pivoting LU in practice).\u0022)\n        for i in range(k \u002B 1, n):\n            L[i, k] = (A[i, k] - np.dot(L[i, :k], U[:k, k])) / U[k, k]\n    return L, U\n\ndef lu_solve(L, U, b):\n    L = _as_float_array(L); U = _as_float_array(U)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = L.shape[0]\n\n    y = np.zeros(n)\n    for i in range(n):\n        y[i] = b[i] - np.dot(L[i, :i], y[:i])\n\n    x = np.zeros(n)\n    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):\n        x[i] = (y[i] - np.dot(U[i, i \u002B 1:], x[i \u002B 1:])) / U[i, i]\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00263\\\\6\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCompute \\(U_{11}=4\\). \\(L_{21}=6/4=1.5\\).  \nThen \\(U_{12}=3\\). \\(U_{22}=3-1.5\\cdot3= -1.5\\).  \nSo:\n\\[\nL=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1.5\u00261\\end{bmatrix},\\quad\nU=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00263\\\\0\u0026-1.5\\end{bmatrix}\n\\]\nFor \\(b=\\begin{bmatrix}10\\\\12\\end{bmatrix}\\):  \nForward: \\(y_1=10\\), \\(y_2=12-1.5\\cdot 10=-3\\).  \nBack: \\(x_2=(-3)/(-1.5)=2\\); \\(x_1=(10-3\\cdot2)/4=1\\).\n\n---\n\n## 3) Cholesky decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor SPD \\(A\\), \\(A=LL^T\\) with \\(L\\) lower triangular:\n$$\nl_{kk}=\\sqrt{a_{kk}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1} l_{ks}^2}\n$$\n$$\nl_{ik}=\\frac{1}{l_{kk}}\\left(a_{ik}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1}l_{is}l_{ks}\\right),\\quad i\u003Ek\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef cholesky_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    L = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        s = np.dot(L[k, :k], L[k, :k])\n        val = A[k, k] - s\n        if val \u003C= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Matrix not SPD.\u0022)\n        L[k, k] = np.sqrt(val)\n        for i in range(k \u002B 1, n):\n            s2 = np.dot(L[i, :k], L[k, :k])\n            L[i, k] = (A[i, k] - s2) / L[k, k]\n    return L\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00262\\\\2\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(l_{11}=\\sqrt{4}=2\\).  \n\\(l_{21}=(2)/2=1\\).  \n\\(l_{22}=\\sqrt{3-1^2}=\\sqrt2\\approx1.4142\\).  \nSo \\(L=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00260\\\\1\u00261.4142\\end{bmatrix}\\).\n\n---\n\n## 4) QR decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nOrthogonal \\(Q\\), upper triangular \\(R\\): \\(A=QR\\), \\(Q^TQ=I\\).  \nClassical Gram–Schmidt:\n$$\nv_k=a_k-\\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(q_j^Ta_k)q_j,\\quad q_k=\\frac{v_k}{\\|v_k\\|}\n$$\nThen \\(R_{jk}=q_j^Ta_k\\).\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef qr_gram_schmidt(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    m, n = A.shape\n    Q = np.zeros((m, n))\n    R = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        v = A[:, k].copy()\n        for j in range(k):\n            R[j, k] = np.dot(Q[:, j], A[:, k])\n            v = v - R[j, k] * Q[:, j]\n        R[k, k] = np.linalg.norm(v)\n        if R[k, k] \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Linearly dependent columns.\u0022)\n        Q[:, k] = v / R[k, k]\n    return Q, R\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00261\\\\1\u00260\\\\0\u00261\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(a_1=(1,1,0)^T\\), \\(\\|a_1\\|=\\sqrt2\\), \\(q_1=(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)\\).  \n\\(R_{12}=q_1^Ta_2=(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot1\u002B(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot0=1/\\sqrt2\\).  \n\\(v_2=a_2-R_{12}q_1=(1,0,1)-(1/\\sqrt2)(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)=(1-1/2,-1/2,1)=(0.5,-0.5,1)\\).  \n\\(\\|v_2\\|=\\sqrt{0.25\u002B0.25\u002B1}= \\sqrt1.5\\).  \nSo \\(q_2=v_2/\\sqrt1.5\\).\n\n---\n\n## 5) SVD\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSingular value decomposition:\n$$\nA=U\\Sigma V^T\n$$\nwhere \\(U,V\\) orthogonal, \\(\\Sigma=\\mathrm{diag}(\\sigma_1\\ge\\cdots\\ge 0)\\).  \nConnection:\n$$\nA^TA = V\\Sigma^2 V^T,\\quad AA^T = U\\Sigma^2 U^T\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef svd_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A, full_matrices=False)\n    Sigma = np.diag(s)\n    return U, Sigma, Vt\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00260\\\\4\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}25\u00260\\\\0\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\Rightarrow \\sigma_1=\\sqrt{25}=5,\\sigma_2=0\\).  \n\\(v_1=(1,0)^T\\).  \nThen \\(u_1=\\frac{Av_1}{\\sigma_1}=\\frac{(3,4)^T}{5}=(0.6,0.8)^T\\).  \nSo \\(A=u_1[5]v_1^T\\).\n\n---\n\n## 6) Eigenvalue decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor diagonalizable \\(A\\):\n$$\nA = V\\Lambda V^{-1},\\quad \\Lambda=\\mathrm{diag}(\\lambda_i)\n$$\nEigenpairs satisfy:\n$$\nA v_i = \\lambda_i v_i\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef eigen_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    w, V = np.linalg.eig(A)\n    Lam = np.diag(w)\n    Vinv = np.linalg.inv(V)\n    return V, Lam, Vinv\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCharacteristic: \\(\\det(A-\\lambda I)=(2-\\lambda)^2-1=\\lambda^2-4\\lambda\u002B3=0\\).  \n\\(\\lambda=3,1\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=3\\): \\((A-3I)v=0\\Rightarrow \\begin{bmatrix}-1\u00261\\\\1\u0026-1\\end{bmatrix}v=0\\Rightarrow v=(1,1)\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=1\\): \\(v=(1,-1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 7) Power iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor dominant eigenpair \\((\\lambda_{\\max},v)\\):\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=\\frac{Ax_k}{\\|Ax_k\\|},\\quad\n\\lambda_k=\\frac{x_k^TAx_k}{x_k^Tx_k}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef power_iteration(A, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.ones(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n    x = x / np.linalg.norm(x)\n\n    lam_old = 0.0\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        y = A @ x\n        x = y / np.linalg.norm(y)\n        lam = float(x.T @ (A @ x))\n        if abs(lam - lam_old) \u003C tol:\n            break\n        lam_old = lam\n    return lam, x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(x_0=(1,0)\\).  \n\\(y_1=Ax_0=(2,1)\\), \\(\\|y_1\\|=\\sqrt5\\), \\(x_1=(2/\\sqrt5,1/\\sqrt5)\\).  \nRayleigh: \\(\\lambda_1=x_1^TAx_1=3 - \\frac{2}{5}=2.6\\) (intermediate value).  \nNext iteration increases toward \\(3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 8) Jacobi iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSplit \\(A=D\u002BL\u002BU\\) (D diagonal). Jacobi:\n$$\nx^{(k\u002B1)} = D^{-1}\\bigl(b-(L\u002BU)x^{(k)}\\bigr)\n$$\nComponent form:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\\ne i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef jacobi_iteration(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    D = np.diag(A)\n    R = A - np.diagflat(D)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = (b - R @ x) / D\n        if _norm_inf(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve:\n\\(\\;10x\u002By=11,\\; x\u002B10y=11\\). Start \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(x_1^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\), \\(y^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nNext: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\), \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\). Converges to \\((1,1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 9) Gauss–Seidel method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nUse newest values immediately:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\u003Ci}a_{ij}x_j^{(k\u002B1)}-\\sum_{j\u003Ei}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef gauss_seidel(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_old = x.copy()\n        for i in range(n):\n            s1 = np.dot(A[i, :i], x[:i])\n            s2 = np.dot(A[i, i\u002B1:], x_old[i\u002B1:])\n            x[i] = (b[i] - s1 - s2) / A[i, i]\n        if _norm_inf(x - x_old) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSame system \\(10x\u002By=11,\\;x\u002B10y=11\\), \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \nIter1: \\(x^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nThen \\(y^{(1)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\).  \nIter2: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-0.99)/10=1.001\\); \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.001)/10=0.9999\\). Faster than Jacobi.\n\n---\n\n## 10) Conjugate gradient method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSolve SPD \\(Ax=b\\) minimizing:\n$$\nf(x)=\\frac12 x^TAx-b^Tx,\\quad \\nabla f = Ax-b=-r\n$$\nIteration (common form):\n$$\nr_0=b-Ax_0,\\; p_0=r_0\n$$\n$$\n\\alpha_k=\\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\\quad x_{k\u002B1}=x_k\u002B\\alpha_k p_k\n$$\n$$\nr_{k\u002B1}=r_k-\\alpha_kAp_k,\\quad\n\\beta_k=\\frac{r_{k\u002B1}^Tr_{k\u002B1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\\quad\np_{k\u002B1}=r_{k\u002B1}\u002B\\beta_k p_k\n$$\n(See standard derivations and discussions in CG references.) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivation_of_the_conjugate_gradient_method)[4](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake-papers/painless-conjugate-gradient.pdf)[7](https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee364b/lectures/conj_grad_slides.pdf)\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef conjugate_gradient(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    r = b - A @ x\n    p = r.copy()\n    rs_old = float(r @ r)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        Ap = A @ p\n        alpha = rs_old / float(p @ Ap)\n        x = x \u002B alpha * p\n        r = r - alpha * Ap\n        rs_new = float(r @ r)\n        if np.sqrt(rs_new) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n        beta = rs_new / rs_old\n        p = r \u002B beta * p\n        rs_old = rs_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00261\\\\1\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2)\\), \\(x_0=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(r_0=b=(1,2)\\), \\(p_0=r_0\\).  \n\\(Ap_0=(4*1\u002B1*2,\\;1*1\u002B3*2)=(6,7)\\).  \n\\(\\alpha_0=(r_0^Tr_0)/(p_0^TAp_0)=(1^2\u002B2^2)/(1*6\u002B2*7)=5/20=0.25\\).  \n\\(x_1=(0,0)\u002B0.25(1,2)=(0.25,0.5)\\).  \n\\(r_1=r_0-\\alpha_0Ap_0=(1,2)-0.25(6,7)=(1-1.5,\\;2-1.75)=(-0.5,0.25)\\).  \nContinue similarly; in exact arithmetic CG solves 2×2 in ≤2 steps.\n\n---\n\n## 11) Least squares fitting\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nGiven \\(A\\in\\mathbb{R}^{m\\times n}\\), minimize \\(\\|Ax-b\\|_2^2\\).  \nNormal equations:\n$$\nA^TAx=A^Tb\n$$\nQR approach (preferred numerically):\n$$\nA=QR,\\quad \\min \\|QRx-b\\| \\Rightarrow Rx=Q^Tb\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef least_squares_qr(A, b):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    Q, R = np.linalg.qr(A, mode=\u0022reduced\u0022)\n    y = Q.T @ b\n    x = np.linalg.solve(R, y)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFit line \\(y\\approx c_0\u002Bc_1x\\) to points \\((0,1),(1,2),(2,2)\\).  \n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2,2)\\).  \nCompute \\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(A^Tb=(5,6)\\).  \nSolve:\n\\(\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\begin{bmatrix}c_0\\\\c_1\\end{bmatrix}=\\begin{bmatrix}5\\\\6\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nEliminate: row2-row1 ⇒ \\(2c_1=1\\Rightarrow c_1=0.5\\).  \nThen \\(3c_0\u002B3*0.5=5\\Rightarrow 3c_0=3.5\\Rightarrow c_0=1.1667\\).\n\n---\n\n# Root Finding\n\n## 12) Bisection method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nIf \\(f(a)f(b)\u003C0\\), root in \\([a,b]\\). Midpoint \\(c=(a\u002Bb)/2\\).  \nShrink interval based on sign:\n$$\n(a,b)\\leftarrow\n\\begin{cases}\n(a,c),\u0026 f(a)f(c)\u003C0\\\\\n(c,b),\u0026 f(c)f(b)\u003C0\n\\end{cases}\n$$\nError bound after \\(n\\) steps:\n$$\n|x^*-c_n|\\le \\frac{b-a}{2^{n\u002B1}}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef bisection(f, a, b, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)\n    if fa * fb \u003E 0:\n        raise ValueError(\u0022f(a) and f(b) must have opposite signs.\u0022)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        c = 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n        fc = f(c)\n        if abs(fc) \u003C tol or 0.5 * (b - a) \u003C tol:\n            return c\n        if fa * fc \u003C 0:\n            b, fb = c, fc\n        else:\n            a, fa = c, fc\n    return 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFind root of \\(f(x)=x^2-2\\) on \\([1,2]\\).  \n\\(f(1)=-1\\), \\(f(2)=2\\).  \n1) \\(c=1.5\\), \\(f(c)=0.25\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1,1.5]\\)  \n2) \\(c=1.25\\), \\(f=-0.4375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.25,1.5]\\)  \n3) \\(c=1.375\\), \\(f=-0.109375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.5]\\)  \n4) \\(c=1.4375\\), \\(f=0.06640625\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.4375]\\) … converges to \\(\\sqrt2\\).\n\n---\n\n## 13) Newton–Raphson\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nLinearize:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{f(x_k)}{f\u0027(x_k)}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef newton_raphson(f, df, x0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        fx = f(x)\n        dfx = df(x)\n        if abs(dfx) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Derivative too small.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx / dfx\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(f\u0027(x)=2x\\), start \\(x_0=1.5\\).  \n\\(x_1=1.5-\\frac{0.25}{3}=1.4166667\\).  \n\\(f(x_1)=1.4166667^2-2=0.0069444\\).  \n\\(x_2=1.4166667-\\frac{0.0069444}{2.8333334}=1.4142157\\).\n\n---\n\n## 14) Secant method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nApproximate derivative by secant slope:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-f(x_k)\\frac{x_k-x_{k-1}}{f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef secant(f, x0, x1, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    x_prev, x = float(x0), float(x1)\n    f_prev, fx = f(x_prev), f(x)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        denom = fx - f_prev\n        if abs(denom) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Zero secant slope.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx * (x - x_prev) / denom\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x_prev, f_prev = x, fx\n        x, fx = x_new, f(x_new)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(x_0=1\\), \\(x_1=2\\).  \n\\(x_2=2-2\\cdot(2-1)/(2-(-1))=2-2/3=1.3333333\\).  \n\\(f(x_2)=-0.2222222\\).  \n\\(x_3=1.3333333-(-0.2222)(1.3333-2)/(-0.2222-2)=1.4\\).\n\n---\n\n## 15) Fixed-point iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nRewrite \\(x=g(x)\\). Iterate:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=g(x_k)\n$$\nConverges if \\(|g\u0027(x^*)|\u003C1\\) near fixed point.\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef fixed_point(g, x0, max_iter=500, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = float(g(x))\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve \\(x=\\cos x\\). Take \\(g(x)=\\cos x\\), \\(x_0=1\\).  \n\\(x_1=\\cos1=0.5403023\\)  \n\\(x_2=\\cos0.5403023=0.8575532\\)  \n\\(x_3=\\cos0.8575532=0.6542898\\) … converges to ~0.739085.\n\n---\n\n## 16) Müller\u0027s method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nQuadratic through \\((x_{k-2},f_{k-2}), (x_{k-1},f_{k-1}), (x_k,f_k)\\).  \nLet \\(h_1=x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}\\), \\(h_2=x_k-x_{k-1}\\),\n$$\n\\delta_1=\\frac{f_{k-1}-f_{k-2}}{h_1},\\quad\n\\delta_2=\\frac{f_k-f_{k-1}}{h_2}\n$$\n$$\nd=\\frac{\\delta_2-\\delta_1}{h_2\u002Bh_1},\\quad\nb=\\delta_2\u002Bh_2 d,\\quad\nD=\\sqrt{b^2-4 f_k d}\n$$\nChoose denominator with larger magnitude:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{2f_k}{b\\pm D}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef muller(f, x0, x1, x2, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x0, x1, x2 = float(x0), float(x1), float(x2)\n    f0, f1, f2 = f(x0), f(x1), f(x2)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        h1, h2 = x1 - x0, x2 - x1\n        d1 = (f1 - f0) / h1\n        d2 = (f2 - f1) / h2\n        d = (d2 - d1) / (h1 \u002B h2)\n        b = d2 \u002B h2 * d\n        D = np.sqrt(b*b - 4.0*f2*d \u002B 0j)  # allow complex\n        denom = b \u002B D if abs(b \u002B D) \u003E abs(b - D) else b - D\n        if abs(denom) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Denominator too small.\u0022)\n        dx = -2.0 * f2 / denom\n        x3 = x2 \u002B dx\n        if abs(dx) \u003C tol:\n            return x3\n        x0, x1, x2 = x1, x2, x3\n        f0, f1, f2 = f1, f2, f(x2)\n    return x2\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example (first step)\n\\(f(x)=x^3-x-1\\), guesses \\(x_0=1\\), \\(x_1=1.5\\), \\(x_2=1.2\\).  \n\\(f_0=-1\\), \\(f_1=0.875\\), \\(f_2=-0.472\\).  \n\\(h_1=0.5\\), \\(h_2=-0.3\\).  \n\\(\\delta_1=(0.875-(-1))/0.5=3.75\\).  \n\\(\\delta_2=(-0.472-0.875)/(-0.3)=4.49\\).  \n\\(d=(4.49-3.75)/(0.2)=3.7\\).  \n\\(b=\\delta_2\u002Bh_2 d=4.49\u002B(-0.3)(3.7)=3.38\\).  \nThen compute \\(D\\) and update \\(x_3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 17) Brent\u0027s method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nBrent combines **bisection** (guaranteed bracketing) with **secant/inverse quadratic interpolation** (fast). \nSo:\n\\[\nL=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1.5\u00261\\end{bmatrix},\\quad\nU=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00263\\\\0\u0026-1.5\\end{bmatrix}\n\\]\nFor \\(b=\\begin{bmatrix}10\\\\12\\end{bmatrix}\\):  \nForward: \\(y_1=10\\), \\(y_2=12-1.5\\cdot 10=-3\\).  \nBack: \\(x_2=(-3)/(-1.5)=2\\); \\(x_1=(10-3\\cdot2)/4=1\\).\n\n---\n\n## 3) Cholesky decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor SPD \\(A\\), \\(A=LL^T\\) with \\(L\\) lower triangular:\n$$\nl_{kk}=\\sqrt{a_{kk}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1} l_{ks}^2}\n$$\n$$\nl_{ik}=\\frac{1}{l_{kk}}\\left(a_{ik}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1}l_{is}l_{ks}\\right),\\quad i\u003Ek\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef cholesky_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    L = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        s = np.dot(L[k, :k], L[k, :k])\n        val = A[k, k] - s\n        if val \u003C= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Matrix not SPD.\u0022)\n        L[k, k] = np.sqrt(val)\n        for i in range(k \u002B 1, n):\n            s2 = np.dot(L[i, :k], L[k, :k])\n            L[i, k] = (A[i, k] - s2) / L[k, k]\n    return L\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00262\\\\2\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(l_{11}=\\sqrt{4}=2\\).  \n\\(l_{21}=(2)/2=1\\).  \n\\(l_{22}=\\sqrt{3-1^2}=\\sqrt2\\approx1.4142\\).  \nSo \\(L=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00260\\\\1\u00261.4142\\end{bmatrix}\\).\n\n---\n\n## 4) QR decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nOrthogonal \\(Q\\), upper triangular \\(R\\): \\(A=QR\\), \\(Q^TQ=I\\).  \nClassical Gram–Schmidt:\n$$\nv_k=a_k-\\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(q_j^Ta_k)q_j,\\quad q_k=\\frac{v_k}{\\|v_k\\|}\n$$\nThen \\(R_{jk}=q_j^Ta_k\\).\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef qr_gram_schmidt(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    m, n = A.shape\n    Q = np.zeros((m, n))\n    R = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        v = A[:, k].copy()\n        for j in range(k):\n            R[j, k] = np.dot(Q[:, j], A[:, k])\n            v = v - R[j, k] * Q[:, j]\n        R[k, k] = np.linalg.norm(v)\n        if R[k, k] \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Linearly dependent columns.\u0022)\n        Q[:, k] = v / R[k, k]\n    return Q, R\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00261\\\\1\u00260\\\\0\u00261\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(a_1=(1,1,0)^T\\), \\(\\|a_1\\|=\\sqrt2\\), \\(q_1=(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)\\).  \n\\(R_{12}=q_1^Ta_2=(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot1\u002B(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot0=1/\\sqrt2\\).  \n\\(v_2=a_2-R_{12}q_1=(1,0,1)-(1/\\sqrt2)(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)=(1-1/2,-1/2,1)=(0.5,-0.5,1)\\).  \n\\(\\|v_2\\|=\\sqrt{0.25\u002B0.25\u002B1}= \\sqrt1.5\\).  \nSo \\(q_2=v_2/\\sqrt1.5\\).\n\n---\n\n## 5) SVD\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSingular value decomposition:\n$$\nA=U\\Sigma V^T\n$$\nwhere \\(U,V\\) orthogonal, \\(\\Sigma=\\mathrm{diag}(\\sigma_1\\ge\\cdots\\ge 0)\\).  \nConnection:\n$$\nA^TA = V\\Sigma^2 V^T,\\quad AA^T = U\\Sigma^2 U^T\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef svd_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A, full_matrices=False)\n    Sigma = np.diag(s)\n    return U, Sigma, Vt\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00260\\\\4\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}25\u00260\\\\0\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\Rightarrow \\sigma_1=\\sqrt{25}=5,\\sigma_2=0\\).  \n\\(v_1=(1,0)^T\\).  \nThen \\(u_1=\\frac{Av_1}{\\sigma_1}=\\frac{(3,4)^T}{5}=(0.6,0.8)^T\\).  \nSo \\(A=u_1[5]v_1^T\\).\n\n---\n\n## 6) Eigenvalue decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor diagonalizable \\(A\\):\n$$\nA = V\\Lambda V^{-1},\\quad \\Lambda=\\mathrm{diag}(\\lambda_i)\n$$\nEigenpairs satisfy:\n$$\nA v_i = \\lambda_i v_i\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef eigen_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    w, V = np.linalg.eig(A)\n    Lam = np.diag(w)\n    Vinv = np.linalg.inv(V)\n    return V, Lam, Vinv\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCharacteristic: \\(\\det(A-\\lambda I)=(2-\\lambda)^2-1=\\lambda^2-4\\lambda\u002B3=0\\).  \n\\(\\lambda=3,1\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=3\\): \\((A-3I)v=0\\Rightarrow \\begin{bmatrix}-1\u00261\\\\1\u0026-1\\end{bmatrix}v=0\\Rightarrow v=(1,1)\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=1\\): \\(v=(1,-1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 7) Power iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor dominant eigenpair \\((\\lambda_{\\max},v)\\):\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=\\frac{Ax_k}{\\|Ax_k\\|},\\quad\n\\lambda_k=\\frac{x_k^TAx_k}{x_k^Tx_k}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef power_iteration(A, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.ones(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n    x = x / np.linalg.norm(x)\n\n    lam_old = 0.0\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        y = A @ x\n        x = y / np.linalg.norm(y)\n        lam = float(x.T @ (A @ x))\n        if abs(lam - lam_old) \u003C tol:\n            break\n        lam_old = lam\n    return lam, x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(x_0=(1,0)\\).  \n\\(y_1=Ax_0=(2,1)\\), \\(\\|y_1\\|=\\sqrt5\\), \\(x_1=(2/\\sqrt5,1/\\sqrt5)\\).  \nRayleigh: \\(\\lambda_1=x_1^TAx_1=3 - \\frac{2}{5}=2.6\\) (intermediate value).  \nNext iteration increases toward \\(3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 8) Jacobi iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSplit \\(A=D\u002BL\u002BU\\) (D diagonal). Jacobi:\n$$\nx^{(k\u002B1)} = D^{-1}\\bigl(b-(L\u002BU)x^{(k)}\\bigr)\n$$\nComponent form:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\\ne i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef jacobi_iteration(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    D = np.diag(A)\n    R = A - np.diagflat(D)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = (b - R @ x) / D\n        if _norm_inf(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve:\n\\(\\;10x\u002By=11,\\; x\u002B10y=11\\). Start \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(x_1^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\), \\(y^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nNext: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\), \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\). Converges to \\((1,1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 9) Gauss–Seidel method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nUse newest values immediately:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\u003Ci}a_{ij}x_j^{(k\u002B1)}-\\sum_{j\u003Ei}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef gauss_seidel(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_old = x.copy()\n        for i in range(n):\n            s1 = np.dot(A[i, :i], x[:i])\n            s2 = np.dot(A[i, i\u002B1:], x_old[i\u002B1:])\n            x[i] = (b[i] - s1 - s2) / A[i, i]\n        if _norm_inf(x - x_old) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSame system \\(10x\u002By=11,\\;x\u002B10y=11\\), \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \nIter1: \\(x^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nThen \\(y^{(1)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\).  \nIter2: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-0.99)/10=1.001\\); \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.001)/10=0.9999\\). Faster than Jacobi.\n\n---\n\n## 10) Conjugate gradient method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSolve SPD \\(Ax=b\\) minimizing:\n$$\nf(x)=\\frac12 x^TAx-b^Tx,\\quad \\nabla f = Ax-b=-r\n$$\nIteration (common form):\n$$\nr_0=b-Ax_0,\\; p_0=r_0\n$$\n$$\n\\alpha_k=\\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\\quad x_{k\u002B1}=x_k\u002B\\alpha_k p_k\n$$\n$$\nr_{k\u002B1}=r_k-\\alpha_kAp_k,\\quad\n\\beta_k=\\frac{r_{k\u002B1}^Tr_{k\u002B1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\\quad\np_{k\u002B1}=r_{k\u002B1}\u002B\\beta_k p_k\n$$\n(See standard derivations and discussions in CG references.) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivation_of_the_conjugate_gradient_method)[4](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake-papers/painless-conjugate-gradient.pdf)[7](https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee364b/lectures/conj_grad_slides.pdf)\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef conjugate_gradient(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    r = b - A @ x\n    p = r.copy()\n    rs_old = float(r @ r)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        Ap = A @ p\n        alpha = rs_old / float(p @ Ap)\n        x = x \u002B alpha * p\n        r = r - alpha * Ap\n        rs_new = float(r @ r)\n        if np.sqrt(rs_new) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n        beta = rs_new / rs_old\n        p = r \u002B beta * p\n        rs_old = rs_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00261\\\\1\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2)\\), \\(x_0=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(r_0=b=(1,2)\\), \\(p_0=r_0\\).  \n\\(Ap_0=(4*1\u002B1*2,\\;1*1\u002B3*2)=(6,7)\\).  \n\\(\\alpha_0=(r_0^Tr_0)/(p_0^TAp_0)=(1^2\u002B2^2)/(1*6\u002B2*7)=5/20=0.25\\).  \n\\(x_1=(0,0)\u002B0.25(1,2)=(0.25,0.5)\\).  \n\\(r_1=r_0-\\alpha_0Ap_0=(1,2)-0.25(6,7)=(1-1.5,\\;2-1.75)=(-0.5,0.25)\\).  \nContinue similarly; in exact arithmetic CG solves 2×2 in ≤2 steps.\n\n---\n\n## 11) Least squares fitting\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nGiven \\(A\\in\\mathbb{R}^{m\\times n}\\), minimize \\(\\|Ax-b\\|_2^2\\).  \nNormal equations:\n$$\nA^TAx=A^Tb\n$$\nQR approach (preferred numerically):\n$$\nA=QR,\\quad \\min \\|QRx-b\\| \\Rightarrow Rx=Q^Tb\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef least_squares_qr(A, b):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    Q, R = np.linalg.qr(A, mode=\u0022reduced\u0022)\n    y = Q.T @ b\n    x = np.linalg.solve(R, y)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFit line \\(y\\approx c_0\u002Bc_1x\\) to points \\((0,1),(1,2),(2,2)\\).  \n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2,2)\\).  \nCompute \\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(A^Tb=(5,6)\\).  \nSolve:\n\\(\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\begin{bmatrix}c_0\\\\c_1\\end{bmatrix}=\\begin{bmatrix}5\\\\6\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nEliminate: row2-row1 ⇒ \\(2c_1=1\\Rightarrow c_1=0.5\\).  \nThen \\(3c_0\u002B3*0.5=5\\Rightarrow 3c_0=3.5\\Rightarrow c_0=1.1667\\).\n\n---\n\n# Root Finding\n\n## 12) Bisection method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nIf \\(f(a)f(b)\u003C0\\), root in \\([a,b]\\). Midpoint \\(c=(a\u002Bb)/2\\).  \nShrink interval based on sign:\n$$\n(a,b)\\leftarrow\n\\begin{cases}\n(a,c),\u0026 f(a)f(c)\u003C0\\\\\n(c,b),\u0026 f(c)f(b)\u003C0\n\\end{cases}\n$$\nError bound after \\(n\\) steps:\n$$\n|x^*-c_n|\\le \\frac{b-a}{2^{n\u002B1}}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef bisection(f, a, b, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)\n    if fa * fb \u003E 0:\n        raise ValueError(\u0022f(a) and f(b) must have opposite signs.\u0022)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        c = 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n        fc = f(c)\n        if abs(fc) \u003C tol or 0.5 * (b - a) \u003C tol:\n            return c\n        if fa * fc \u003C 0:\n            b, fb = c, fc\n        else:\n            a, fa = c, fc\n    return 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFind root of \\(f(x)=x^2-2\\) on \\([1,2]\\).  \n\\(f(1)=-1\\), \\(f(2)=2\\).  \n1) \\(c=1.5\\), \\(f(c)=0.25\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1,1.5]\\)  \n2) \\(c=1.25\\), \\(f=-0.4375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.25,1.5]\\)  \n3) \\(c=1.375\\), \\(f=-0.109375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.5]\\)  \n4) \\(c=1.4375\\), \\(f=0.06640625\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.4375]\\) … converges to \\(\\sqrt2\\).\n\n---\n\n## 13) Newton–Raphson\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nLinearize:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{f(x_k)}{f\u0027(x_k)}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef newton_raphson(f, df, x0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        fx = f(x)\n        dfx = df(x)\n        if abs(dfx) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Derivative too small.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx / dfx\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(f\u0027(x)=2x\\), start \\(x_0=1.5\\).  \n\\(x_1=1.5-\\frac{0.25}{3}=1.4166667\\).  \n\\(f(x_1)=1.4166667^2-2=0.0069444\\).  \n\\(x_2=1.4166667-\\frac{0.0069444}{2.8333334}=1.4142157\\).\n\n---\n\n## 14) Secant method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nApproximate derivative by secant slope:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-f(x_k)\\frac{x_k-x_{k-1}}{f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef secant(f, x0, x1, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    x_prev, x = float(x0), float(x1)\n    f_prev, fx = f(x_prev), f(x)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        denom = fx - f_prev\n        if abs(denom) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Zero secant slope.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx * (x - x_prev) / denom\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x_prev, f_prev = x, fx\n        x, fx = x_new, f(x_new)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(x_0=1\\), \\(x_1=2\\).  \n\\(x_2=2-2\\cdot(2-1)/(2-(-1))=2-2/3=1.3333333\\).  \n\\(f(x_2)=-0.2222222\\).  \n\\(x_3=1.3333333-(-0.2222)(1.3333-2)/(-0.2222-2)=1.4\\).\n\n---\n\n## 15) Fixed-point iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nRewrite \\(x=g(x)\\). Iterate:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=g(x_k)\n$$\nConverges if \\(|g\u0027(x^*)|\u003C1\\) near fixed point.\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef fixed_point(g, x0, max_iter=500, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = float(g(x))\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve \\(x=\\cos x\\). Take \\(g(x)=\\cos x\\), \\(x_0=1\\).  \n\\(x_1=\\cos1=0.5403023\\)  \n\\(x_2=\\cos0.5403023=0.8575532\\)  \n\\(x_3=\\cos0.8575532=0.6542898\\) … converges to ~0.739085.\n\n---\n\n## 16) Müller\u0027s method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nQuadratic through \\((x_{k-2},f_{k-2}), (x_{k-1},f_{k-1}), (x_k,f_k)\\).  \nLet \\(h_1=x_{k-1}-x_{k-2}\\), \\(h_2=x_k-x_{k-1}\\),\n$$\n\\delta_1=\\frac{f_{k-1}-f_{k-2}}{h_1},\\quad\n\\delta_2=\\frac{f_k-f_{k-1}}{h_2}\n$$\n$$\nd=\\frac{\\delta_2-\\delta_1}{h_2\u002Bh_1},\\quad\nb=\\delta_2\u002Bh_2 d,\\quad\nD=\\sqrt{b^2-4 f_k d}\n$$\nChoose denominator with larger magnitude:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{2f_k}{b\\pm D}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef muller(f, x0, x1, x2, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x0, x1, x2 = float(x0), float(x1), float(x2)\n    f0, f1, f2 = f(x0), f(x1), f(x2)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        h1, h2 = x1 - x0, x2 - x1\n        d1 = (f1 - f0) / h1\n        d2 = (f2 - f1) / h2\n        d = (d2 - d1) / (h1 \u002B h2)\n        b = d2 \u002B h2 * d\n        D = np.sqrt(b*b - 4.0*f2*d \u002B 0j)  # allow complex\n        denom = b \u002B D if abs(b \u002B D) \u003E abs(b - D) else b - D\n        if abs(denom) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Denominator too small.\u0022)\n        dx = -2.0 * f2 / denom\n        x3 = x2 \u002B dx\n        if abs(dx) \u003C tol:\n            return x3\n        x0, x1, x2 = x1, x2, x3\n        f0, f1, f2 = f1, f2, f(x2)\n    return x2\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example (first step)\n\\(f(x)=x^3-x-1\\), guesses \\(x_0=1\\), \\(x_1=1.5\\), \\(x_2=1.2\\).  \n\\(f_0=-1\\), \\(f_1=0.875\\), \\(f_2=-0.472\\).  \n\\(h_1=0.5\\), \\(h_2=-0.3\\).  \n\\(\\delta_1=(0.875-(-1))/0.5=3.75\\).  \n\\(\\delta_2=(-0.472-0.875)/(-0.3)=4.49\\).  \n\\(d=(4.49-3.75)/(0.2)=3.7\\).  \n\\(b=\\delta_2\u002Bh_2 d=4.49\u002B(-0.3)(3.7)=3.38\\).  \nThen compute \\(D\\) and update \\(x_3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 17) Brent\u0027s method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nBrent combines **bisection** (guaranteed bracketing) with **secant/inverse quadratic interpolation** (fast). Maintain bracket \\([a,b]\\) with \\(f(a)f(b)\u003C0\\); propose IQI/secant step if “safe,” otherwise bisection.\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef brent(f, a, b, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    a, b = float(a), float(b)\n    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)\n    if fa * fb \u003E 0:\n        raise ValueError(\u0022Root must be bracketed.\u0022)\n    c, fc = a, fa\n    d = e = b - a\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        if abs(fc) \u003C abs(fb):\n            a, b, c = b, c, b\n            fa, fb, fc = fb, fc, fb\n\n        tol1 = 2*np.finfo(float).eps*abs(b) \u002B 0.5*tol\n        m = 0.5*(c - b)\n        if abs(m) \u003C= tol1 or fb == 0:\n            return b\n\n        if abs(e) \u003E= tol1 and abs(fa) \u003E abs(fb):\n            s = fb / fa\n            if a == c:\n                p = 2*m*s\n                q = 1 - s\n            else:\n                q = fa / fc\n                r = fb / fc\n                p = s*(2*m*q*(q - r) - (b - a)*(r - 1))\n                q = (q - 1)*(r - 1)*(s - 1)\n            if p \u003E 0:\n                q = -q\n            p = abs(p)\n            if 2*p \u003C min(3*m*q - abs(tol1*q), abs(e*q)):\n                e, d = d, p / q\n            else:\n                e, d = d, m\n        else:\n            e, d = d, m\n\n        a, fa = b, fb\n        b = b \u002B (d if abs(d) \u003E tol1 else (tol1 if m \u003E 0 else -tol1))\n        fb = f(b)\n        if fb * fc \u003E 0:\n            c, fc = a, fa\n            d = e = b - a\n    return b\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example (key intermediates)\nSame \\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), bracket \\([1,2]\\). Brent will:\n- keep bracket sign change,\n- attempt secant \\(x\\approx 1.3333\\),\n- fall back to bisection when interpolation step would leave bracket,\n- converge quickly to \\(1.41421356\\).\n\n---\n\n# Interpolation\n\n## 18) Lagrange interpolation\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nGiven nodes \\((x_i,y_i)\\):\n$$\np(x)=\\sum_{i=0}^n y_i \\ell_i(x),\\quad\n\\ell_i(x)=\\prod_{j\\ne i}\\frac{x-x_j}{x_i-x_j}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef lagrange_interpolate(x_nodes, y_nodes, x):\n    x_nodes = _as_float_array(x_nodes).reshape(-1)\n    y_nodes = _as_float_array(y_nodes).reshape(-1)\n    x = float(x)\n    n = len(x_nodes)\n    p = 0.0\n    for i in range(n):\n        li = 1.0\n        for j in range(n):\n            if j != i:\n                li *= (x - x_nodes[j]) / (x_nodes[i] - x_nodes[j])\n        p \u002B= y_nodes[i] * li\n    return p\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nPoints \\((0,1),(1,3),(2,2)\\). Evaluate at \\(x=1.5\\).  \n\\(\\ell_0=(x-1)(x-2)/((0-1)(0-2))=(0.5)(-0.5)/(2)= -0.125\\).  \n\\(\\ell_1=(x-0)(x-2)/((1-0)(1-2))=(1.5)(-0.5)/(-1)=0.75\\).  \n\\(\\ell_2=(x-0)(x-1)/((2-0)(2-1))=(1.5)(0.5)/2=0.375\\).  \n\\(p(1.5)=1(-0.125)\u002B3(0.75)\u002B2(0.375)= -0.125\u002B2.25\u002B0.75=2.875\\).\n\n---\n\n## 19) Newton’s divided differences\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nPolynomial:\n$$\np(x)=c_0\u002Bc_1(x-x_0)\u002Bc_2(x-x_0)(x-x_1)\u002B\\cdots\n$$\nDivided differences:\n$$\nf[x_i]=y_i,\\quad\nf[x_i,\\dots,x_{i\u002Bk}]=\\frac{f[x_{i\u002B1},\\dots,x_{i\u002Bk}]-f[x_i,\\dots,x_{i\u002Bk-1}]}{x_{i\u002Bk}-x_i}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef newton_divided_differences(x_nodes, y_nodes):\n    x = _as_float_array(x_nodes).reshape(-1)\n    coef = _as_float_array(y_nodes).reshape(-1).copy()\n    n = len(x)\n    for j in range(1, n):\n        coef[j:n] = (coef[j:n] - coef[j-1:n-1]) / (x[j:n] - x[0:n-j])\n    return coef\n\ndef newton_eval(x_nodes, coef, x):\n    x_nodes = _as_float_array(x_nodes).reshape(-1)\n    coef = _as_float_array(coef).reshape(-1)\n    x = float(x)\n    n = len(coef)\n    p = coef[-1]\n    for k in range(n - 2, -1, -1):\n        p = coef[k] \u002B (x - x_nodes[k]) * p\n    return p\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSame nodes \\(x=[0,1,2]\\), \\(y=[1,3,2]\\).  \nLevel1: \\(f[x0,x1]=(3-1)/(1-0)=2\\), \\(f[x1,x2]=(2-3)/(2-1)=-1\\).  \nLevel2: \\(f[x0,x1,x2]=(-1-2)/(2-0)=-1.5\\).  \nSo \\(p(x)=1\u002B2(x-0)-1.5(x-0)(x-1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 20) Cubic spline interpolation (natural)\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nPiecewise cubic \\(S_i(x)\\) with continuity of \\(S,S\u0027,S\u0027\u0027\\). \\(Q^TQ=I\\).  \nClassical Gram–Schmidt:\n$$\nv_k=a_k-\\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(q_j^Ta_k)q_j,\\quad q_k=\\frac{v_k}{\\|v_k\\|}\n$$\nThen \\(R_{jk}=q_j^Ta_k\\).\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef qr_gram_schmidt(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    m, n = A.shape\n    Q = np.zeros((m, n))\n    R = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        v Vt\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00260\\\\4\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}25\u00260\\\\0\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\Rightarrow \\sigma_1=\\sqrt{25}=5,\\sigma_2=0\\).  \n\\(v_1=(1,0)^T\\).  \nThen \\(u_1=\\frac{Av_1}{\\sigma_1}=\\frac{(3,4)^T}{5}=(0.6,0.8)^T\\).  \nSo \\(A=u_1[5]v_1^T\\).\n\n---\n\n## 6) Eigenvalue decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor diagonalizable \\(A\\):\n$$\nA = V\\Lambda V^{-1},\\quad \\Lambda=\\mathrm{diag}(\\lambda_i)\n$$\nEigenpairs satisfy:\n$$\nA v_i = \\lambda_i v_i\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef eigen_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    w, V = np.linalg.eig(A)\n    Lam = np.diag(w)\n    Vinv = np.linalg.inv(V)\n    return V, Lam, Vinv\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCharacteristic: \\(\\det(A-\\lambda I)=(2-\\lambda)^2-1=\\lambda^2-4\\lambda\u002B3=0\\).  \n\\(\\lambda=3,1\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=3\\): \\((A-3I)v=0\\Rightarrow \\begin{bmatrix}-1\u00261\\\\1\u0026-1\\end{bmatrix}v=0\\Rightarrow v=(1,1)\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=1\\): \\(v=(1,-1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 7) Power iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor dominant eigenpair \\((\\lambda_{\\max},v)\\):\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=\\frac{Ax_k}{\\|Ax_k\\|},\\quad\n\\lambda_k=\\frac{x_k^TAx_k}{x_k^Tx_k}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef power_iteration(A, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.ones(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n    x = x / np.linalg.norm(x)\n\n    lam_old = 0.0\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        y = A @ x\n        x = y / np.linalg.norm(y)\n        lam = float(x.T @ (A @ x))\n        if abs(lam - lam_old) \u003C tol:\n            break\n        lam_old = lam\n    return lam, x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(x_0=(1,0)\\).  \n\\(y_1=Ax_0=(2,1)\\), \\(\\|y_1\\|=\\sqrt5\\), \\(x_1=(2/\\sqrt5,1/\\sqrt5)\\).  \nRayleigh: \\(\\lambda_1=x_1^TAx_1=3 - \\frac{2}{5}=2.6\\) (intermediate value).  \nNext iteration increases toward \\(3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 8) Jacobi iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSplit \\(A=D\u002BL\u002BU\\) (D diagonal). Jacobi:\n$$\nx^{(k\u002B1)} = D^{-1}\\bigl(b-(L\u002BU)x^{(k)}\\bigr)\n$$\nComponent form:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\\ne i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef jacobi_iteration(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    D = np.diag(A)\n    R = A - np.diagflat(D)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = (b - R @ x) / D\n        if _norm_inf(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve:\n\\(\\;10x\u002By=11,\\; x\u002B10y=11\\). Start \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(x_1^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\), \\(y^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nNext: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\), \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\). Converges to \\((1,1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 9) Gauss–Seidel method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nUse newest values immediately:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\u003Ci}a_{ij}x_j^{(k\u002B1)}-\\sum_{j\u003Ei}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef gauss_seidel(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_old = x.copy()\n        for i in range(n):\n            s1 = np.dot(A[i, :i], x[:i])\n            s2 = np.dot(A[i, i\u002B1:], x_old[i\u002B1:])\n            x[i] = (b[i] - s1 - s2) / A[i, i]\n        if _norm_inf(x - x_old) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSame system \\(10x\u002By=11,\\;x\u002B10y=11\\), \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \nIter1: \\(x^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nThen \\(y^{(1)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\).  \nIter2: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-0.99)/10=1.001\\); \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.001)/10=0.9999\\). Faster than Jacobi.\n\n---\n\n## 10) Conjugate gradient method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSolve SPD \\(Ax=b\\) minimizing:\n$$\nf(x)=\\frac12 x^TAx-b^Tx,\\quad \\nabla f = Ax-b=-r\n$$\nIteration (common form):\n$$\nr_0=b-Ax_0,\\; p_0=r_0\n$$\n$$\n\\alpha_k=\\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\\quad x_{k\u002B1}=x_k\u002B\\alpha_k p_k\n$$\n$$\nr_{k\u002B1}=r_k-\\alpha_kAp_k,\\quad\n\\beta_k=\\frac{r_{k\u002B1}^Tr_{k\u002B1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\\quad\np_{k\u002B1}=r_{k\u002B1}\u002B\\beta_k p_k\n$$\n(See standard derivations and discussions in CG references.) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivation_of_the_conjugate_gradient_method)[4](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake-papers/painless-conjugate-gradient.pdf)[7](https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee364b/lectures/conj_grad_slides.pdf)\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef conjugate_gradient(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    r = b - A @ x\n    p = r.copy()\n    rs_old = float(r @ r)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        Ap = A @ p\n        alpha = rs_old / float(p @ Ap)\n        x = x \u002B alpha * p\n        r = r - alpha * Ap\n        rs_new = float(r @ r)\n        if np.sqrt(rs_new) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n        beta = rs_new / rs_old\n        p = r \u002B beta * p\n        rs_old = rs_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00261\\\\1\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2)\\), \\(x_0=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(r_0=b=(1,2)\\), \\(p_0=r_0\\).  \n\\(Ap_0=(4*1\u002B1*2,\\;1*1\u002B3*2)=(6,7)\\).  \n\\(\\alpha_0=(r_0^Tr_0)/(p_0^TAp_0)=(1^2\u002B2^2)/(1*6\u002B2*7)=5/20=0.25\\).  \n\\(x_1=(0,0)\u002B0.25(1,2)=(0.25,0.5)\\).  \n\\(r_1=r_0-\\alpha_0Ap_0=(1,2)-0.25(6,7)=(1-1.5,\\;2-1.75)=(-0.5,0.25)\\).  \nContinue similarly; in exact arithmetic CG solves 2×2 in ≤2 steps.\n\n---\n\n## 11) Least squares fitting\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nGiven \\(A\\in\\mathbb{R}^{m\\times n}\\), minimize \\(\\|Ax-b\\|_2^2\\).  \nNormal equations:\n$$\nA^TAx=A^Tb\n$$\nQR approach (preferred numerically):\n$$\nA=QR,\\quad \\min \\|QRx-b\\| \\Rightarrow Rx=Q^Tb\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef least_squares_qr(A, b):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    Q, R = np.linalg.qr(A, mode=\u0022reduced\u0022)\n    y = Q.T @ b\n    x = np.linalg.solve(R, y)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFit line \\(y\\approx c_0\u002Bc_1x\\) to points \\((0,1),(1,2),(2,2)\\).  \n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2,2)\\).  \nCompute \\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(A^Tb=(5,6)\\).  \nSolve:\n\\(\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\begin{bmatrix}c_0\\\\c_1\\end{bmatrix}=\\begin{bmatrix}5\\\\6\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nEliminate: row2-row1 ⇒ \\(2c_1=1\\Rightarrow c_1=0.5\\).  \nThen \\(3c_0\u002B3*0.5=5\\Rightarrow 3c_0=3.5\\Rightarrow c_0=1.1667\\).\n\n---\n\n# Root Finding\n\n## 12) Bisection method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nIf \\(f(a)f(b)\u003C0\\), root in \\([a,b]\\). Midpoint \\(c=(a\u002Bb)/2\\).  \nShrink interval based on sign:\n$$\n(a,b)\\leftarrow\n\\begin{cases}\n(a,c),\u0026 f(a)f(c)\u003C0\\\\\n(c,b),\u0026 f(c)f(b)\u003C0\n\\end{cases}\n$$\nError bound after \\(n\\) steps:\n$$\n|x^*-c_n|\\le \\frac{b-a}{2^{n\u002B1}}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef bisection(f, a, b, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)\n    if fa * fb \u003E 0:\n        raise ValueError(\u0022f(a) and f(b) must have opposite signs.\u0022)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        c = 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n        fc = f(c)\n        if abs(fc) \u003C tol or 0.5 * (b - a) \u003C tol:\n            return c\n        if fa * fc \u003C 0:\n            b, fb = c, fc\n        else:\n            a, fa = c, fc\n    return 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFind root of \\(f(x)=x^2-2\\) on \\([1,2]\\).  \n\\(f(1)=-1\\), \\(f(2)=2\\).  \n1) \\(c=1.5\\), \\(f(c)=0.25\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1,1.5]\\)  \n2) \\(c=1.25\\), \\(f=-0.4375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.25,1.5]\\)  \n3) \\(c=1.375\\), \\(f=-0.109375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.5]\\)  \n4) \\(c=1.4375\\), \\(f=0.06640625\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.4375]\\) … converges to \\(\\sqrt2\\).\n\n---\n\n## 13) Newton–Raphson\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nLinearize:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{f(x_k)}{f\u0027(x_k)}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef newton_raphson(f, df, x0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        fx = f(x)\n        dfx = df(x)\n        if abs(dfx) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Derivative too small.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx / dfx\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(f\u0027(x)=2x\\), start \\(x_0=1.5\\).  \n\\(x_1=1.5-\\frac{0.25}{3}=1.4166667\\).  \n\\(f(x_1)=1.4166667^2-2=0.0069444\\).  \n\\(x_2=1.4166667-\\frac{0.0069444}{2.8333334}=1.4142157\\).\n\n---\n\n## 14) Secant method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nApproximate derivative by secant slope:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-f(x_k)\\frac{x_k-x_{k-1}}{f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef secant(f, x0, x1, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    x_prev, x = float(x0), float(x1)\n    f_prev, fx = f(x_prev), f(x)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        denom = fx - f_prev\n        if abs(denom) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Zero secant slope.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx * (x - x_prev) / denom\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x_prev, f_prev = x, fx\n        x, fx = x_new, f(x_new)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(x_0=1\\), \\(x_1=2\\).  \n\\(x_2=2-2\\cdot(2-1)/(2-(-1))=2-2/3=1.3333333\\).  \n\\(f(x_2)=-0.2222222\\).  \n\\(x_3=1.3333333-(-0.2222)(1.3333-2)/(-0.2222-2)=1.4\\).\n\n---\n\n## 15) Fixed-point iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nRewrite \\(x=g(x)\\). Iterate:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=g(x_k)\n$$\nConverges if \\(|g\u0027(x^*)|\u003C1\\) near fixed point.\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef fixed_point(g, x0, max_iter=500, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = float(g(x))\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve \\(x=\\cos x\\). m * Ab[k, k:]\n\n    x = np.zeros(n)\n    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):\n        rhs = Ab[i, -1] - np.dot(Ab[i, i \u002B 1:n], x[i \u002B 1:n])\n        x[i] = rhs / Ab[i, i]\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example (with intermediate values)\nSolve:\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n2x\u002By\u0026=5\\\\\n4x-6y\u0026=-2\n\\end{aligned}\n\\Rightarrow\n\\left[\\begin{array}{cc|c}2\u00261\u00265\\\\4\u0026-6\u0026-2\\end{array}\\right]\n\\]\nEliminate row2 using row1: \\(m_{21}=4/2=2\\).  \nRow2 ← Row2 − 2·Row1:\n\\[\n\\left[\\begin{array}{cc|c}2\u00261\u00265\\\\0\u0026-8\u0026-12\\end{array}\\right]\n\\]\nBack substitute: \\(y=(-12)/(-8)=1.5\\).  \nThen \\(2x\u002B1.5=5\\Rightarrow x=1.75\\).\n\n---\n\n## 2) LU decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFactor \\(A=LU\\) (Doolittle: diag(L)=1). For \\(k\\le j\\):\n$$\nu_{kj}=a_{kj}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1} l_{ks}u_{sj}\n$$\nFor \\(i\u003Ek\\):\n$$\nl_{ik}=\\frac{1}{u_{kk}}\\left(a_{ik}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1}l_{is}u_{sk}\\right)\n$$\nSolve \\(Ly=b\\), then \\(Ux=y\\).\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef lu_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    L = np.eye(n)\n    U = np.zeros((n, n))\n\n    for k in range(n):\n        for j in range(k, n):\n            U[k, j] = A[k, j] - np.dot(L[k, :k], U[:k, j])\n        if abs(U[k, k]) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Zero pivot (use pivoting LU in practice).\u0022)\n        for i in range(k \u002B 1, n):\n            L[i, k] = (A[i, k] - np.dot(L[i, :k], U[:k, k])) / U[k, k]\n    return L, U\n\ndef lu_solve(L, U, b):\n    L = _as_float_array(L); U = _as_float_array(U)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = L.shape[0]\n\n    y = np.zeros(n)\n    for i in range(n):\n        y[i] = b[i] - np.dot(L[i, :i], y[:i])\n\n    x = np.zeros(n)\n    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):\n        x[i] = (y[i] - np.dot(U[i, i \u002B 1:], x[i \u002B 1:])) / U[i, i]\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00263\\\\6\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCompute \\(U_{11}=4\\). \\(L_{21}=6/4=1.5\\).  \nThen \\(U_{12}=3\\). \\(U_{22}=3-1.5\\cdot3= -1.5\\).  \nSo:\n\\[\nL=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1.5\u00261\\end{bmatrix},\\quad\nU=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00263\\\\0\u0026-1.5\\end{bmatrix}\n\\]\nFor \\(b=\\begin{bmatrix}10\\\\12\\end{bmatrix}\\):  \nForward: \\(y_1=10\\), \\(y_2=12-1.5\\cdot 10=-3\\).  \nBack: \\(x_2=(-3)/(-1.5)=2\\); \\(x_1=(10-3\\cdot2)/4=1\\).\n\n---\n\n## 3) Cholesky decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor SPD \\(A\\), \\(A=LL^T\\) with \\(L\\) lower triangular:\n$$\nl_{kk}=\\sqrt{a_{kk}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1} l_{ks}^2}\n$$\n$$\nl_{ik}=\\frac{1}{l_{kk}}\\left(a_{ik}-\\sum_{s=1}^{k-1}l_{is}l_{ks}\\right),\\quad i\u003Ek\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef cholesky_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    L = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        s = np.dot(L[k, :k], L[k, :k])\n        val = A[k, k] - s\n        if val \u003C= 0:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Matrix not SPD.\u0022)\n        L[k, k] = np.sqrt(val)\n        for i in range(k \u002B 1, n):\n            s2 = np.dot(L[i, :k], L[k, :k])\n            L[i, k] = (A[i, k] - s2) / L[k, k]\n    return L\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00262\\\\2\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(l_{11}=\\sqrt{4}=2\\).  \n\\(l_{21}=(2)/2=1\\).  \n\\(l_{22}=\\sqrt{3-1^2}=\\sqrt2\\approx1.4142\\).  \nSo \\(L=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00260\\\\1\u00261.4142\\end{bmatrix}\\).\n\n---\n\n## 4) QR decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nOrthogonal \\(Q\\), upper triangular \\(R\\): \\(A=QR\\), \\(Q^TQ=I\\).  \nClassical Gram–Schmidt:\n$$\nv_k=a_k-\\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(q_j^Ta_k)q_j,\\quad q_k=\\frac{v_k}{\\|v_k\\|}\n$$\nThen \\(R_{jk}=q_j^Ta_k\\).\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef qr_gram_schmidt(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    m, n = A.shape\n    Q = np.zeros((m, n))\n    R = np.zeros((n, n))\n    for k in range(n):\n        v = A[:, k].copy()\n        for j in range(k):\n            R[j, k] = np.dot(Q[:, j], A[:, k])\n            v = v - R[j, k] * Q[:, j]\n        R[k, k] = np.linalg.norm(v)\n        if R[k, k] \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Linearly dependent columns.\u0022)\n        Q[:, k] = v / R[k, k]\n    return Q, R\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00261\\\\1\u00260\\\\0\u00261\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(a_1=(1,1,0)^T\\), \\(\\|a_1\\|=\\sqrt2\\), \\(q_1=(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)\\).  \n\\(R_{12}=q_1^Ta_2=(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot1\u002B(1/\\sqrt2)\\cdot0=1/\\sqrt2\\).  \n\\(v_2=a_2-R_{12}q_1=(1,0,1)-(1/\\sqrt2)(1/\\sqrt2,1/\\sqrt2,0)=(1-1/2,-1/2,1)=(0.5,-0.5,1)\\).  \n\\(\\|v_2\\|=\\sqrt{0.25\u002B0.25\u002B1}= \\sqrt1.5\\).  \nSo \\(q_2=v_2/\\sqrt1.5\\).\n\n---\n\n## 5) SVD\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSingular value decomposition:\n$$\nA=U\\Sigma V^T\n$$\nwhere \\(U,V\\) orthogonal, \\(\\Sigma=\\mathrm{diag}(\\sigma_1\\ge\\cdots\\ge 0)\\).  \nConnection:\n$$\nA^TA = V\\Sigma^2 V^T,\\quad AA^T = U\\Sigma^2 U^T\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef svd_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A, full_matrices=False)\n    Sigma = np.diag(s)\n    return U, Sigma, Vt\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00260\\\\4\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \n\\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}25\u00260\\\\0\u00260\\end{bmatrix}\\Rightarrow \\sigma_1=\\sqrt{25}=5,\\sigma_2=0\\).  \n\\(v_1=(1,0)^T\\).  \nThen \\(u_1=\\frac{Av_1}{\\sigma_1}=\\frac{(3,4)^T}{5}=(0.6,0.8)^T\\).  \nSo \\(A=u_1[5]v_1^T\\).\n\n---\n\n## 6) Eigenvalue decomposition\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor diagonalizable \\(A\\):\n$$\nA = V\\Lambda V^{-1},\\quad \\Lambda=\\mathrm{diag}(\\lambda_i)\n$$\nEigenpairs satisfy:\n$$\nA v_i = \\lambda_i v_i\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef eigen_decomposition(A):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    w, V = np.linalg.eig(A)\n    Lam = np.diag(w)\n    Vinv = np.linalg.inv(V)\n    return V, Lam, Vinv\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nCharacteristic: \\(\\det(A-\\lambda I)=(2-\\lambda)^2-1=\\lambda^2-4\\lambda\u002B3=0\\).  \n\\(\\lambda=3,1\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=3\\): \\((A-3I)v=0\\Rightarrow \\begin{bmatrix}-1\u00261\\\\1\u0026-1\\end{bmatrix}v=0\\Rightarrow v=(1,1)\\).  \nFor \\(\\lambda=1\\): \\(v=(1,-1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 7) Power iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nFor dominant eigenpair \\((\\lambda_{\\max},v)\\):\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=\\frac{Ax_k}{\\|Ax_k\\|},\\quad\n\\lambda_k=\\frac{x_k^TAx_k}{x_k^Tx_k}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef power_iteration(A, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.ones(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n    x = x / np.linalg.norm(x)\n\n    lam_old = 0.0\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        y = A @ x\n        x = y / np.linalg.norm(y)\n        lam = float(x.T @ (A @ x))\n        if abs(lam - lam_old) \u003C tol:\n            break\n        lam_old = lam\n    return lam, x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}2\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(x_0=(1,0)\\).  \n\\(y_1=Ax_0=(2,1)\\), \\(\\|y_1\\|=\\sqrt5\\), \\(x_1=(2/\\sqrt5,1/\\sqrt5)\\).  \nRayleigh: \\(\\lambda_1=x_1^TAx_1=3 - \\frac{2}{5}=2.6\\) (intermediate value).  \nNext iteration increases toward \\(3\\).\n\n---\n\n## 8) Jacobi iteration\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSplit \\(A=D\u002BL\u002BU\\) (D diagonal). Jacobi:\n$$\nx^{(k\u002B1)} = D^{-1}\\bigl(b-(L\u002BU)x^{(k)}\\bigr)\n$$\nComponent form:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\\ne i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef jacobi_iteration(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    D = np.diag(A)\n    R = A - np.diagflat(D)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_new = (b - R @ x) / D\n        if _norm_inf(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSolve:\n\\(\\;10x\u002By=11,\\; x\u002B10y=11\\). Start \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(x_1^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\), \\(y^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nNext: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\), \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\). Converges to \\((1,1)\\).\n\n---\n\n## 9) Gauss–Seidel method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nUse newest values immediately:\n$$\nx_i^{(k\u002B1)}=\\frac{1}{a_{ii}}\\left(b_i-\\sum_{j\u003Ci}a_{ij}x_j^{(k\u002B1)}-\\sum_{j\u003Ei}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}\\right)\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef gauss_seidel(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=500, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        x_old = x.copy()\n        for i in range(n):\n            s1 = np.dot(A[i, :i], x[:i])\n            s2 = np.dot(A[i, i\u002B1:], x_old[i\u002B1:])\n            x[i] = (b[i] - s1 - s2) / A[i, i]\n        if _norm_inf(x - x_old) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nSame system \\(10x\u002By=11,\\;x\u002B10y=11\\), \\(x^{(0)}=(0,0)\\).  \nIter1: \\(x^{(1)}=(11-0)/10=1.1\\).  \nThen \\(y^{(1)}=(11-1.1)/10=0.99\\).  \nIter2: \\(x^{(2)}=(11-0.99)/10=1.001\\); \\(y^{(2)}=(11-1.001)/10=0.9999\\). Faster than Jacobi.\n\n---\n\n## 10) Conjugate gradient method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nSolve SPD \\(Ax=b\\) minimizing:\n$$\nf(x)=\\frac12 x^TAx-b^Tx,\\quad \\nabla f = Ax-b=-r\n$$\nIteration (common form):\n$$\nr_0=b-Ax_0,\\; p_0=r_0\n$$\n$$\n\\alpha_k=\\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{p_k^TAp_k},\\quad x_{k\u002B1}=x_k\u002B\\alpha_k p_k\n$$\n$$\nr_{k\u002B1}=r_k-\\alpha_kAp_k,\\quad\n\\beta_k=\\frac{r_{k\u002B1}^Tr_{k\u002B1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\\quad\np_{k\u002B1}=r_{k\u002B1}\u002B\\beta_k p_k\n$$\n(See standard derivations and discussions in CG references.) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivation_of_the_conjugate_gradient_method)[4](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake-papers/painless-conjugate-gradient.pdf)[7](https://web.stanford.edu/class/ee364b/lectures/conj_grad_slides.pdf)\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef conjugate_gradient(A, b, x0=None, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-10):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    n = A.shape[0]\n    x = np.zeros(n) if x0 is None else _as_float_array(x0).reshape(-1)\n\n    r = b - A @ x\n    p = r.copy()\n    rs_old = float(r @ r)\n\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        Ap = A @ p\n        alpha = rs_old / float(p @ Ap)\n        x = x \u002B alpha * p\n        r = r - alpha * Ap\n        rs_new = float(r @ r)\n        if np.sqrt(rs_new) \u003C tol:\n            return x\n        beta = rs_new / rs_old\n        p = r \u002B beta * p\n        rs_old = rs_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}4\u00261\\\\1\u00263\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2)\\), \\(x_0=(0,0)\\).  \n\\(r_0=b=(1,2)\\), \\(p_0=r_0\\).  \n\\(Ap_0=(4*1\u002B1*2,\\;1*1\u002B3*2)=(6,7)\\).  \n\\(\\alpha_0=(r_0^Tr_0)/(p_0^TAp_0)=(1^2\u002B2^2)/(1*6\u002B2*7)=5/20=0.25\\).  \n\\(x_1=(0,0)\u002B0.25(1,2)=(0.25,0.5)\\).  \n\\(r_1=r_0-\\alpha_0Ap_0=(1,2)-0.25(6,7)=(1-1.5,\\;2-1.75)=(-0.5,0.25)\\).  \nContinue similarly; in exact arithmetic CG solves 2×2 in ≤2 steps.\n\n---\n\n## 11) Least squares fitting\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nGiven \\(A\\in\\mathbb{R}^{m\\times n}\\), minimize \\(\\|Ax-b\\|_2^2\\).  \nNormal equations:\n$$\nA^TAx=A^Tb\n$$\nQR approach (preferred numerically):\n$$\nA=QR,\\quad \\min \\|QRx-b\\| \\Rightarrow Rx=Q^Tb\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef least_squares_qr(A, b):\n    A = _as_float_array(A)\n    b = _as_float_array(b).reshape(-1)\n    Q, R = np.linalg.qr(A, mode=\u0022reduced\u0022)\n    y = Q.T @ b\n    x = np.linalg.solve(R, y)\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFit line \\(y\\approx c_0\u002Bc_1x\\) to points \\((0,1),(1,2),(2,2)\\).  \n\\(A=\\begin{bmatrix}1\u00260\\\\1\u00261\\\\1\u00262\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(b=(1,2,2)\\).  \nCompute \\(A^TA=\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\), \\(A^Tb=(5,6)\\).  \nSolve:\n\\(\\begin{bmatrix}3\u00263\\\\3\u00265\\end{bmatrix}\\begin{bmatrix}c_0\\\\c_1\\end{bmatrix}=\\begin{bmatrix}5\\\\6\\end{bmatrix}\\).  \nEliminate: row2-row1 ⇒ \\(2c_1=1\\Rightarrow c_1=0.5\\).  \nThen \\(3c_0\u002B3*0.5=5\\Rightarrow 3c_0=3.5\\Rightarrow c_0=1.1667\\).\n\n---\n\n# Root Finding\n\n## 12) Bisection method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nIf \\(f(a)f(b)\u003C0\\), root in \\([a,b]\\). Midpoint \\(c=(a\u002Bb)/2\\).  \nShrink interval based on sign:\n$$\n(a,b)\\leftarrow\n\\begin{cases}\n(a,c),\u0026 f(a)f(c)\u003C0\\\\\n(c,b),\u0026 f(c)f(b)\u003C0\n\\end{cases}\n$$\nError bound after \\(n\\) steps:\n$$\n|x^*-c_n|\\le \\frac{b-a}{2^{n\u002B1}}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef bisection(f, a, b, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    fa, fb = f(a), f(b)\n    if fa * fb \u003E 0:\n        raise ValueError(\u0022f(a) and f(b) must have opposite signs.\u0022)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        c = 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n        fc = f(c)\n        if abs(fc) \u003C tol or 0.5 * (b - a) \u003C tol:\n            return c\n        if fa * fc \u003C 0:\n            b, fb = c, fc\n        else:\n            a, fa = c, fc\n    return 0.5 * (a \u002B b)\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\nFind root of \\(f(x)=x^2-2\\) on \\([1,2]\\).  \n\\(f(1)=-1\\), \\(f(2)=2\\).  \n1) \\(c=1.5\\), \\(f(c)=0.25\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1,1.5]\\)  \n2) \\(c=1.25\\), \\(f=-0.4375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.25,1.5]\\)  \n3) \\(c=1.375\\), \\(f=-0.109375\u003C0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.5]\\)  \n4) \\(c=1.4375\\), \\(f=0.06640625\u003E0\\Rightarrow [1.375,1.4375]\\) … converges to \\(\\sqrt2\\).\n\n---\n\n## 13) Newton–Raphson\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nLinearize:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-\\frac{f(x_k)}{f\u0027(x_k)}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef newton_raphson(f, df, x0, max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):\n    x = float(x0)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        fx = f(x)\n        dfx = df(x)\n        if abs(dfx) \u003C 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\u0022Derivative too small.\u0022)\n        x_new = x - fx / dfx\n        if abs(x_new - x) \u003C tol:\n            return x_new\n        x = x_new\n    return x\n\u0060\u0060\u0060\n\n### Worked example\n\\(f(x)=x^2-2\\), \\(f\u0027(x)=2x\\), start \\(x_0=1.5\\).  \n\\(x_1=1.5-\\frac{0.25}{3}=1.4166667\\).  \n\\(f(x_1)=1.4166667^2-2=0.0069444\\).  \n\\(x_2=1.4166667-\\frac{0.0069444}{2.8333334}=1.4142157\\).\n\n---\n\n## 14) Secant method\n\n### Mathematical foundation\nApproximate derivative by secant slope:\n$$\nx_{k\u002B1}=x_k-f(x_k)\\frac{x_k-x_{k-1}}{f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})}\n$$\n\n### Python implementation\n\u0060\u0060\u0060python\ndef secant(f, x0, x1, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12):\n    x_prev, x = float(x0), float(x1)\n    f_prev, fx = f(x_prev), f(x)\n    for _ in range(max_iter):\n        denom = fx -
